intent.raw_query: Cambodia Angkor Wat + beaches, $1100, 10 days, November 2026

selected_hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

experiences.name: Angkor Wat Temple Complex Sunrise Tour
experiences.description: Explore the world's largest religious monument at sunrise, wandering through ancient Khmer temples including Angkor Thom, Bayon, and Ta Prohm. Hire a local tuk-tuk driver for a full-day small circuit tour to absorb centuries of history and intricate stone carvings.

experiences.name: Phnom Penh Historical & Cultural Day
experiences.description: Visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda to admire Khmer royal architecture, then pay respects at the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum and Choeung Ek Memorial to understand Cambodia's complex modern history. A deeply moving and essential cultural experience.

experiences.name: Koh Rong Samloem Beach Escape
experiences.description: Take a ferry to the pristine island of Koh Rong Samloem and spend the day on Saracen Bay or Lazy Beach, with crystal-clear turquoise waters and powdery white sand. Snorkel the coral reefs, spot bioluminescent plankton at night, and enjoy fresh seafood at beachside shacks.
experiences.location: Koh Rong Samloem Island, Sihanoukville Province

experiences.name: Siem Reap Khmer Cooking Class
experiences.description: Join a hands-on cooking class led by a local chef at a traditional Cambodian home or cooking school. Learn to prepare authentic dishes like Fish Amok, Lok Lak, and Khmer red curry using fresh ingredients sourced from the Phsar Leu local market visited at the start of the class.

experiences.name: Kampot River & Pepper Plantation Tour
experiences.description: Cruise along the Kampot River on a sunset boat tour, passing French colonial architecture and lush countryside. Visit a world-renowned Kampot pepper plantation to learn about the cultivation of one of Cambodia's most prized exports, and sample fresh pepper with local snacks.
experiences.location: Kampot Riverside & Kep Pepper Farms, Kampot Province

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - Cambodia
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: No morning activities — flight arrives at 13:00. Rest and transit time.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and arrange a tuk-tuk to your boutique stay in the Angkor Archaeological Park area (budget ~$5–7 USD). Check in, freshen up, and take a slow walk around the immediate neighborhood to get oriented. Visit the nearby Angkor Night Market area in the late afternoon to browse stalls and get a feel for the city.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chas) area. Explore the lively atmosphere, browse street food vendors, and enjoy the vibrant local scene without spending much. Pick up a cold Angkor beer ($1) from a local shop and soak in the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight meal or airport snack
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at the airport or a roadside stall near your hotel upon arrival. Try a bowl of Kuy Teav (rice noodle soup) for ~$1.50 at a local eatery.
meals.dinner: Eat at a local Khmer restaurant near Pub Street. Try Amok (fish curry in coconut milk) or Lok Lak (stir-fried beef) for $3–5. Recommended: Khmer Kitchen Restaurant for authentic local food at budget prices.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD to Khmer Riel at the airport or a local money changer for small purchases. USD is widely accepted in Cambodia. Negotiate tuk-tuk fares before boarding. Keep your first evening light as jet lag may kick in.

day_by_day.morning: Rise before dawn (4:30 AM) and hire a tuk-tuk (~$15 for a full-day Angkor pass tour) to witness the iconic sunrise over Angkor Wat. Arrive by 5:15 AM to secure a good spot at the reflecting pool. Watch the sun rise behind the temple towers — one of the most breathtaking sights in Southeast Asia. Spend the morning exploring Angkor Wat's interior: the bas-reliefs depicting Hindu epics, the central sanctuary, and the galleries. Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62 USD) at the ticket office — best value for multiple days of temple exploration.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom, the ancient walled city. Visit the Bayon Temple with its famous 216 enigmatic stone faces, then explore the Baphuon Temple, the Elephant Terrace, and the Terrace of the Leper King. Walk or cycle between sites to save money.
day_by_day.evening: Return to your hotel to rest and freshen up. Head to the Siem Reap Night Market for souvenir shopping (bargain hard!) and street food. Watch a free traditional Apsara dance performance sometimes offered at local restaurants with dinner.

meals.breakfast: Pack snacks from a local convenience store the night before (bread, bananas ~$1). Eat at the temple complex food stalls — fried rice or noodles for $2.
meals.lunch: Eat at one of the local food stalls just outside the Angkor Thom gates. Rice with grilled chicken or pork for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Try the Night Market food court near Sivatha Boulevard. A full meal of grilled meats, rice, and a drink costs $3–4.

day_by_day.notes: Bring plenty of water (buy a large bottle for $0.50), sunscreen, and a hat — November is generally dry season but still warm (~28–32°C). Wear modest clothing to enter temple sanctuaries (shoulders and knees covered). Rent a bicycle near your hotel for $2–3/day to navigate temple complexes independently.

day_by_day.morning: Use your Angkor Pass (Day 2) to explore the remote and atmospheric Ta Prohm temple — famously known as the 'Tomb Raider temple' where giant tree roots engulf ancient stone walls. Arrive early (7:00 AM) before tour groups arrive for a more serene experience. Spend 1.5–2 hours wandering the jungle-clad ruins.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Kdei, a Buddhist temple complex just 500m from Ta Prohm, then head to Srah Srang, a royal bathing pool with beautiful views. In the late afternoon, cycle or tuk-tuk to Banteay Srei (~30 km north of Siem Reap) — a stunning 10th-century temple renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings of Hindu deities. It's considered one of the finest examples of Khmer art.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap and visit the Angkor National Museum ($12 entry) if budget allows, or opt for the free outdoor exhibit areas near the museum. Explore the area around the Old French Quarter for a quieter evening walk.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local Khmer breakfast shop near your hotel. Bai Sach Chrouk (grilled pork over rice) is a classic Cambodian breakfast for $1.50–2.
meals.lunch: Pack lunch from a local market or eat at temple food stalls. Rice, vegetables, and grilled meat for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Try Marum Restaurant (training restaurant supporting at-risk youth) — 3-course Khmer meals for $6–8. Excellent quality and a meaningful way to spend your money.

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is covered by your Angkor Pass. A round-trip tuk-tuk to Banteay Srei costs ~$15–20 — consider sharing with other travelers to split costs. The carvings at Banteay Srei are incredibly detailed; bring a good camera.

day_by_day.morning: Use your Angkor Pass (Day 3 — final day) to visit the lesser-known but equally impressive Preah Khan temple — a large flat complex with long corridors, stone faces, and jungle atmosphere similar to Ta Prohm but far fewer crowds. Spend 2 hours exploring. Then visit Neak Pean, a small artificial island temple in the middle of a reservoir, and Ta Som, a compact jungle temple with a beautiful tree-covered eastern gopura.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the floating villages on Tonlé Sap Lake — the largest freshwater lake in Southeast Asia. Take a local boat tour (~$10–15 per person) to see the fascinating stilted and floating villages where communities live entirely on water. Visit Kampong Phluk or Chong Kneas village. The lake landscape changes dramatically with the seasons.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Siem Reap and relax. Visit Wat Bo, a beautiful local pagoda with well-preserved 19th-century murals depicting the Ramayana — free entry and far fewer tourists than Angkor sites.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local café near the hotel. French baguette with pâté (a colonial legacy) and iced coffee for $2 — widely available in Siem Reap.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Tonlé Sap lakeside — fresh grilled fish straight from the lake for $3–4 at local stalls.
meals.dinner: Cook Street Food Crawl: spend $4–5 sampling various street foods around the Old Market area — spring rolls ($0.50), grilled corn ($0.50), fresh fruit shakes ($1), and Num Banh Chok (Khmer noodles, $1.50).

day_by_day.notes: The Tonlé Sap boat tour prices vary — negotiate at the dock. Avoid operators near the main tourist areas; walk a bit further for local prices. Be aware that some floating village tours can feel exploitative; choose community-run operators where possible.

day_by_day.morning: Take an early morning bus from Siem Reap to Phnom Penh (the capital). Book a budget bus ticket with Giant Ibis, Mekong Express, or Capitol Tours ($10–15 USD, ~6 hours). Depart around 7:00–7:30 AM. Enjoy the countryside scenery of rural Cambodia through the window.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh around 1:00–2:00 PM. Check into a budget guesthouse in the BKK1 or Riverside area ($8–15/night for a clean dorm or private room). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda complex ($10 entry) — a stunning example of Khmer architecture with glittering spires, a Throne Hall, and a Silver Pagoda floor made of 5,000 silver tiles. Dress modestly.
day_by_day.evening: Walk along the Sisowath Quay (Riverside Promenade) as the sun sets over the Mekong and Tonlé Sap rivers. The riverfront is lively with locals, vendors, and cafés. Visit the Night Market along the riverfront for affordable street food and local handicrafts.

meals.breakfast: Eat before departure at your Siem Reap hotel or grab road snacks at the bus station ($1–2).
meals.lunch: Eat at a roadside stop during the bus journey or upon arrival in Phnom Penh at a local market stall ($2–3).
meals.dinner: Eat at a Khmer local restaurant on the Riverside. Try Samlor Machu (sour soup) and steamed rice for $3–4. Foreign Correspondents' Club (FCC) rooftop has great views but slightly higher prices ($6–8) — worth it for the atmosphere one evening.

day_by_day.notes: Book your bus ticket in advance online or at your Siem Reap hotel. Giant Ibis is the most reliable and comfortable budget option. Store valuables securely during the bus journey. Phnom Penh is a larger, busier city — be more cautious with bag snatching on motos.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21) — a former high school turned Khmer Rouge prison and torture center ($3 entry). This deeply moving and important historical site documents the atrocities of the Pol Pot regime (1975–1979). Allocate at least 2 hours. The audio guide ($3 extra) is highly recommended for context.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take a tuk-tuk (~$8–10 return) to the Choeung Ek Killing Fields (~15 km from city center, $6 entry including audio guide). This is the most significant memorial site of the Cambodian genocide where over 17,000 people were executed. The audio guide is essential and deeply respectful. Spend 1.5–2 hours here. Return to the city and visit Wat Phnom — the founding temple of Phnom Penh, set on a small hill ($1 donation).
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco building from 1937 with a large yellow dome. Browse handicrafts, jewelry, and clothing stalls. Great for budget souvenir shopping.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local Phnom Penh breakfast spot. Nom Banh Chok (rice noodles with fish gravy) or Kuy Teav for $1.50 near your guesthouse.
meals.lunch: Eat near Tuol Sleng at a local Khmer restaurant — rice and curry for $2–3.
meals.dinner: Try the Street 240 'restaurant row' area for a mix of local and international budget options. Khmer BBQ (cook-your-own meat and seafood) for $5–7 per person is fun and filling.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy. Take your time, be respectful, and allow yourself space to process what you see. These sites are crucial for understanding Cambodia's recent history. Dress modestly and speak quietly.

day_by_day.morning: Visit the National Museum of Cambodia ($10 entry) — one of the finest collections of Khmer art in the world, housed in a beautiful traditional red-painted building. See sculptures, ceramics, and bronzes spanning 2,000 years of Khmer civilization. Spend 1.5–2 hours here.
day_by_day.afternoon: Explore the BKK1 neighborhood and the Russian Market (Psar Tuol Tom Poung) — a large covered market selling everything from silk scarves and handicrafts to electronics and clothing. Great for budget shopping. Bargain confidently. In the late afternoon, take a free sunset walk along the Mekong Riverside and watch local families play and exercise along the promenade.
day_by_day.evening: Book a budget overnight bus or early morning bus to Kampot for the next day. Spend the evening at a rooftop bar near the Riverside for one splurge drink with a view (~$3–4 for a local beer). Pack your bag for tomorrow's travel.

meals.breakfast: Eat at a local bakery or café near your guesthouse. Cambodian iced coffee (Ca Phe) and a pastry for $2.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Russian Market food court — fresh noodles, rice dishes, and local snacks for $1.50–2. Authentic and delicious.
meals.dinner: Try Romdeng Restaurant (another training restaurant supporting marginalized youth) — Khmer cuisine with a twist for $6–8. Try the tarantula appetizer if you're adventurous ($3 extra)!

day_by_day.notes: Book your Phnom Penh to Kampot bus ticket today for tomorrow morning. Giant Ibis or Mekong Express runs this route ($8–10, ~3 hours). Check out of your Phnom Penh guesthouse tonight or arrange a late checkout.

day_by_day.morning: Take the morning bus from Phnom Penh to Kampot (depart ~7:00–8:00 AM, arrive ~10:30–11:00 AM). Kampot is a charming, laid-back riverside town in southern Cambodia, known for its French colonial architecture, pepper farms, and proximity to beaches. Check into a budget guesthouse or riverside bungalow ($8–15/night). Take a slow walk through the Old Town and along the Kampot River to get oriented.
day_by_day.afternoon: Rent a bicycle ($2–3/day) or motorbike ($7–10/day) and explore the surrounding countryside. Visit a Kampot pepper farm — Kampot pepper is world-famous and farm tours are often free or $2–3. See the pepper vines, taste different varieties (black, red, white), and buy some to take home as a gift. Cycle through rice paddies and small villages for an authentic rural Cambodia experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot town and enjoy the relaxed riverside atmosphere. Kampot is famous for its sunsets over the Elephant Mountains. Grab a drink at a riverside bar and watch the sky turn orange and pink. The town has a great backpacker vibe without being overwhelming.

meals.breakfast: Eat on the bus or at the Phnom Penh bus station before departure ($1–2).
meals.lunch: Eat at a local Khmer restaurant in Kampot Old Town upon arrival. Fresh river fish with rice for $2.50–3.
meals.dinner: Try the Kampot Riverside Night Food Market for fresh grilled seafood, BBQ, and local dishes. A full meal with drinks for $4–6.

day_by_day.notes: Kampot is one of Cambodia's most pleasant towns — take it slow and enjoy the pace. The town is very walkable and bikeable. November is the beginning of dry season in this region — expect warm, mostly sunny weather (~28–30°C). Kampot pepper farm visits are a highlight — don't miss them.

day_by_day.morning: Take a tuk-tuk or local bus (~$1.50, 30 minutes) from Kampot to Kep — a small, quiet seaside town with a fascinating colonial history. Kep was once a glamorous French resort town and later destroyed during the Khmer Rouge era. Explore the Kep National Park hiking trails (free entry) through jungle to hilltop viewpoints with panoramic views of the Gulf of Thailand and offshore islands.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kep Beach — a small but pleasant beach with calm, clear waters. Spend 2–3 hours swimming, relaxing, and soaking up the sun. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market on the seafront — a row of wooden stalls selling freshly caught crabs cooked in Kampot pepper sauce (a local specialty). This is a must-eat experience.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot by tuk-tuk or local bus. Spend your last evening in Kampot exploring the small bar scene along the riverside. Try a locally brewed craft beer or a Khmer rum cocktail at one of the budget-friendly bars. Pack your bags for the final leg of the trip.

meals.breakfast: Eat at your Kampot guesthouse or a local café. Banana pancakes with honey and iced coffee — a classic backpacker breakfast for $2–3.
meals.lunch: Eat at the Kep Crab Market — a whole crab cooked in Kampot pepper sauce with rice costs $6–8. Splurge-worthy and utterly delicious. This is one of Cambodia's signature culinary experiences.
meals.dinner: Eat at a local Kampot restaurant. Try Lok Lak (shaking beef) or Khmer fish amok for $3–4 with rice and a local beer.

day_by_day.notes: Kep is small and best explored by bicycle or tuk-tuk. The crab market lunch is worth the slight splurge — it's a unique Cambodian experience. Kep National Park trails range from easy to moderate; wear good shoes. The beach at Kep is not Cambodia's best but is peaceful and uncrowded.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up early and take one final sunrise walk or bicycle ride along the Kampot River — one of the most peaceful and photogenic scenes in Cambodia. Visit the Kampot Old Town one last time to pick up any remaining souvenirs: Kampot pepper, palm sugar, local handicrafts, and silk scarves make great gifts. Browse the morning market (Psar Kampot) for fresh tropical fruits and local snacks to take on your journey.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the bus back to Phnom Penh ($8–10, ~3 hours, depart ~9:00–10:00 AM to arrive by early afternoon) or directly to Sihanoukville if you have a flight from there. If returning to Phnom Penh for a flight, use the afternoon to revisit any missed spots or relax at a riverside café. If time allows, visit Wat Ounalom — the headquarters of Cambodian Buddhism, located on the Riverside — for free.
day_by_day.evening: Final dinner in Cambodia. Treat yourself to a slightly nicer Khmer meal to celebrate the trip. Try a restaurant in Phnom Penh's Riverside area or BKK1 neighborhood. Reflect on 10 incredible days of temples, history, culture, and beaches. Head to the airport for your departure flight.

meals.breakfast: Final Cambodian breakfast at a local Kampot eatery. Bai Sach Chrouk (grilled pork rice) or Nom Banh Chok for $1.50–2.
meals.lunch: Eat on the bus or at a roadside stop. Pack snacks from the morning market in Kampot ($1–2).
meals.dinner: Farewell dinner at a mid-range Khmer restaurant in Phnom Penh. A full meal with drinks for $6–10. Try Malis Restaurant for upscale Khmer cuisine at reasonable prices, or stick to local spots for $4–5.

day_by_day.notes: Confirm your departure flight details and arrange airport transport in advance (tuk-tuk ~$8–10 from city center to Phnom Penh airport). Arrive at the airport at least 2.5 hours before international departure. Keep some USD for airport taxes or last-minute purchases. Cambodia has been an incredible journey — budget travelers can experience the full depth of this country for under $40–50 USD per day including accommodation, food, transport, and entry fees.

trip_options.title: Classic Cambodia Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and settle in.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check into your boutique stay near Angkor Archaeological Park. After freshening up, take a gentle orientation walk around the hotel grounds and nearby Angkor Village area. Visit the nearby Angkor National Museum (about 15 minutes away) for a compelling introduction to Khmer history, art, and the Angkor civilization — perfect for setting the context for the days ahead.
day_by_day.evening: Head to Pub Street and the Old Market (Psar Chas) area for a relaxed first evening. Stroll through the night market stalls, browse local handicrafts, and soak in the lively atmosphere of central Siem Reap.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Light meal at the airport or grab a quick bite at a café near the hotel upon arrival (try Café Central or a hotel café)
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant on Pub Street — authentic Cambodian cuisine at mid-range prices. Try amok fish curry and lok lak beef. Budget: $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Exchange some USD or withdraw Cambodian Riel (KHR) at the airport or an ATM near the hotel. USD is widely accepted in Siem Reap. Purchase a 3-day Angkor Pass ($62) at the Angkor ticket office before it closes — it opens until 17:30. This will save time tomorrow morning.

day_by_day.morning: Rise early (pre-dawn, around 05:00) for the iconic Angkor Wat sunrise. Watch the sun rise over the world's largest religious monument reflected in the lotus pond — an unforgettable experience. Spend the morning (until around 09:30) exploring Angkor Wat's galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and climbing to the upper levels for panoramic views.
day_by_day.afternoon: After a mid-morning break, visit Angkor Thom — the great walled city. Explore the South Gate with its iconic naga balustrades, the Bayon Temple with its 216 serene stone faces, the Baphuon, and the Terrace of the Elephants. Take your time wandering this magnificent complex.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel to rest and refresh. Head to Siem Reap town center for dinner and a traditional Apsara dance performance — a classical Khmer art form recognized by UNESCO.

meals.breakfast: Early light snack or coffee before sunrise (pack a granola bar from the hotel). After Angkor Wat, have a proper breakfast at one of the open-air cafés near the park entrance — try Angkor Café or a local noodle stall (kuy teav soup). Budget: $3–5.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a local restaurant near Angkor Thom — try Khmer Kitchen or a roadside stall for bai sach chrouk (pork and rice). Budget: $5–8.
meals.dinner: Dinner and Apsara show at Koulen II Restaurant or Smile of Angkor — set dinner with traditional dance performance. Budget: $18–25 per person including show.

day_by_day.notes: Dress modestly at temple sites — shoulders and knees must be covered. Bring sunscreen, a hat, and plenty of water. The November weather should be pleasant and dry — ideal temple-visiting conditions. Hire a tuk-tuk driver for the day (approximately $15–20) for convenient temple hopping.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the jungle temples of the Angkor complex. Begin with Ta Prohm — the atmospheric 'Tomb Raider' temple where massive silk-cotton trees have grown through and around the ancient stone structures. Then visit Preah Khan, a sprawling temple-monastery with long columned corridors and peaceful courtyards.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Banteay Srei — a stunning 10th-century temple located about 25 km north of Siem Reap, renowned for its intricate pink sandstone carvings considered the finest in all of Angkor. The detailed bas-reliefs of Hindu deities and floral motifs are extraordinary. On the way back, stop at the Landmine Museum — a sobering but important cultural site documenting Cambodia's tragic history with landmines.
day_by_day.evening: Relax with a sunset cruise on Tonle Sap Lake (about 15 km south of Siem Reap). Watch the sun dip below the horizon over Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake, home to floating villages and rich biodiversity.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at your boutique hotel (usually included in mid-range stays) or at a nearby café — try bai sach chrouk or French-influenced baguette with pâté, a Cambodian breakfast staple.
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch near Banteay Srei or at a local restaurant in the area — fresh spring rolls, grilled corn, and coconut water. Budget: $4–7.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak — one of Siem Reap's most celebrated restaurants offering a contemporary Cambodian tasting menu using local seasonal ingredients. Reservation recommended. Budget: $25–35 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei requires a separate tuk-tuk or longer journey — negotiate with your driver for a full-day rate (~$25–30). The Landmine Museum requests a small donation. Your 3-day Angkor Pass remains valid today.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to the Angkor Archaeological Park's lesser-visited gems — Preah Neak Poan, a unique island temple set in a large reservoir, and Ta Som, a small but beautifully preserved temple with a magnificent tree-covered eastern gopura. These quieter sites offer a more serene and intimate experience.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and silk farm at Puok village (about 16 km from Siem Reap). Watch skilled artisans practice traditional Khmer crafts — stone carving, lacquerware, silk weaving, and silver work. This social enterprise trains disadvantaged young Cambodians. Browse the shop for authentic, ethically made souvenirs.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the vibrant Siem Reap Night Market and Angkor Night Market. Shop for silk scarves, Khmer shadow puppets, handmade jewelry, and local art. Enjoy street food from the various food stalls.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or local café — try num banh chok (Khmer noodles with green curry fish sauce), Cambodia's beloved morning dish.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Artisans Angkor café or a nearby local eatery — fresh Khmer food at very reasonable prices. Budget: $5–8.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Haven Restaurant — a social enterprise training vulnerable youth in hospitality. Excellent Khmer and Western fusion food in a warm atmosphere. Budget: $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: This is your last day using the 3-day Angkor Pass. The Artisans Angkor tour is free of charge. Consider purchasing a few items here as gifts — the quality is excellent and your purchase directly supports local artisans.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Siem Reap by early morning bus or minivan to Phnom Penh (approximately 5–6 hours by road, or 1 hour by domestic flight if budget allows). Giant Ibis or Mekong Express are reliable, comfortable bus options (~$12–15). Enjoy the Cambodian countryside scenery en route.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive in Phnom Penh early-to-mid afternoon. Check into a mid-range hotel in the riverside area (BKK1 or Riverside districts recommended). After settling in, visit the Royal Palace and Silver Pagoda — the stunning royal residence featuring gilded spires, elaborate murals, and the famous Silver Pagoda with its emerald Buddha and solid silver floor tiles.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Phnom Penh Riverside promenade (Sisowath Quay) as the sun sets over the Tonle Sap and Mekong rivers. Watch locals gather for evening exercise and socializing — a lovely slice of everyday Cambodian life.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at the hotel before departure — or grab food at Siem Reap bus station.
meals.lunch: Lunch stop during the bus journey or at a roadside restaurant — local rice dishes or noodle soups. Budget: $3–6.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Friends Restaurant (Mith Samlanh) on the Riverside — another excellent social enterprise training street youth, with creative Cambodian tapas-style dishes. Budget: $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book bus tickets in advance, especially for the popular Siem Reap–Phnom Penh route. Store valuables securely while traveling. Phnom Penh accommodation recommendation: Pavilion Hotel or The Plantation Urban Resort for mid-range comfort (~$60–90/night).

day_by_day.morning: Visit the Tuol Sleng Genocide Museum (S-21 Prison) — a deeply moving and essential historical site. The former high school was used as a torture and interrogation center by the Khmer Rouge between 1975–1979. Understanding this history is crucial to comprehending modern Cambodia. Allow 2–3 hours and consider hiring an audio guide or local survivor guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Choeung Ek Genocidal Center (The Killing Fields), located about 15 km south of the city. This memorial site features a striking Buddhist stupa filled with the skulls of victims and peaceful memorial grounds. The audio guide (included in entry) is narrated by survivors and is extraordinarily powerful. Afterward, take time to decompress at a riverside café.
day_by_day.evening: Explore the Central Market (Psar Thmei) — a stunning Art Deco building from 1937 with a large yellow dome. Browse stalls selling jewelry, clothing, electronics, and local goods. Then enjoy a sunset cocktail at a rooftop bar overlooking the Mekong.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a local café near the hotel — try nom pang (Cambodian baguette sandwich) from a street vendor, a delicious French colonial legacy. Budget: $1–2.
meals.lunch: Light lunch after the museum visits — Romdeng Restaurant serves traditional Cambodian dishes including exotic Khmer cuisine (deep-fried tarantulas for the adventurous!). Budget: $8–12.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Topaz Restaurant — elegant French-Cambodian fusion in a beautiful colonial setting. A treat for a special evening. Budget: $20–30 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Tuol Sleng and Choeung Ek visits are emotionally heavy — be prepared and take breaks as needed. Photography is permitted but should be done respectfully. Combined entry fees are approximately $6–9 per site. These visits are historically essential and deeply humanizing.

day_by_day.morning: Morning visit to Wat Phnom — the hilltop temple that gives Phnom Penh its name. Explore the beautifully decorated stupa and pagoda, watch monks in prayer, and enjoy views over the city. Then visit the National Museum of Cambodia — a magnificent terracotta-colored building housing the world's finest collection of Khmer art and sculpture, including pre-Angkorian bronzes and stunning sandstone statues.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depart Phnom Penh for Kampot — a charming riverside colonial town in southern Cambodia, approximately 3–4 hours by bus or minivan. Check into a mid-range guesthouse along the Kampot River. After settling in, rent a bicycle and explore Kampot's quiet streets lined with French colonial architecture, pepper farms, and riverside cafés.
day_by_day.evening: Enjoy Kampot's famously laid-back evening atmosphere. Take a sunset boat cruise on the Kampot River — watch fireflies emerge along the riverbanks as darkness falls. A truly magical experience unique to this region.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast in Phnom Penh or a local bakery — fresh croissants and coffee reflect the French colonial influence.
meals.lunch: Lunch in Phnom Penh before departure or a roadside stop — bun (rice vermicelli) with various toppings. Budget: $3–5.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Rikitikitavi or Rusty Keyhole in Kampot — popular riverside restaurants with excellent Khmer and international food, cold Angkor beer, and beautiful river views. Budget: $8–14 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book Phnom Penh to Kampot transport in advance via Giant Ibis or Cambolink (~$10–12). Kampot is famous for its pepper — considered among the world's finest. Buy some at a local farm shop as a souvenir. Kampot accommodation recommendation: Les Manguiers or Mea Culpa Hotel (~$40–70/night).

day_by_day.morning: Take a morning tuk-tuk tour to a Kampot pepper farm — La Plantation or Sothy's Pepper Farm offer guided tours explaining the cultivation and processing of the celebrated Kampot pepper (a Geographical Indication product). Taste different varieties — black, red, and white. Then visit Phnom Chhngok Cave Temple — a beautiful limestone cave containing a 7th-century brick sanctuary. The surrounding countryside scenery is stunning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to Kep — a small seaside resort town just 25 km from Kampot, once a glamorous French colonial retreat. Explore the atmospheric ruins of abandoned colonial villas overgrown with jungle. Visit the famous Kep Crab Market — a string of seafood shacks on stilts over the water where you can choose your own fresh crab to be cooked with Kampot pepper — a legendary local dish.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Kampot for the evening. Enjoy a relaxing sunset from one of the riverside bars — Naga House or Epic Arts Café are popular spots with great atmosphere and cold drinks.

meals.breakfast: Breakfast at a Kampot riverside café — fresh fruit, yogurt, and Cambodian coffee (strong iced coffee with condensed milk). Budget: $3–5.
meals.lunch: Lunch at the Kep Crab Market — fresh crab with Kampot pepper sauce, grilled fish, and steamed clams. An unmissable culinary experience. Budget: $10–15 per person.
meals.dinner: Dinner at Chhay Seavmey or a local Khmer restaurant in Kampot — simple, fresh, and delicious. Budget: $6–10 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Rent a bicycle or motorbike in Kampot for the day (~$3–7) — it's the best way to explore the area at your own pace. The Kep Crab Market is busiest at lunchtime. November weather in this region should be warm, dry, and pleasant — perfect for outdoor exploration.

day_by_day.morning: Depart Kampot early for Sihanoukville port, then take a ferry to Koh Rong Samloem — one of Cambodia's most beautiful islands, known for its pristine white sand beaches, crystal-clear turquoise waters, and laid-back atmosphere. The ferry takes approximately 45 minutes to 1.5 hours. Check into a mid-range beach bungalow on Saracen Bay or M'Pai Bay.
day_by_day.afternoon: Spend the afternoon relaxing on the stunning beaches of Koh Rong Samloem. Swim in the warm, clear waters, snorkel around the coral reefs, or simply lounge under a palm tree with a good book. Rent a kayak to explore hidden coves and the island's jungle-covered interior.
day_by_day.evening: After sunset, experience one of Cambodia's most magical natural phenomena — bioluminescent plankton in the sea. Swim or wade in the dark water and watch the water light up with electric blue sparks around your movements. This is best experienced on calm, dark nights away from artificial light.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast in Kampot or Sihanoukville before the ferry — grab a nom pang or fruit smoothie.
meals.lunch: Lunch at a beachfront restaurant on Koh Rong Samloem — fresh grilled fish, coconut curry, or simple fried rice. Budget: $6–10.
meals.dinner: Dinner at a beach bungalow restaurant on Saracen Bay — fresh seafood barbecue under the stars. Budget: $10–15 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Ferry tickets from Sihanoukville to Koh Rong Samloem: approximately $20–25 round trip. Book in advance during peak season. The island has limited ATMs — bring sufficient cash. Accommodation recommendation: Sunset Bungalows or The Beach Club (~$50–80/night). The bioluminescence is best seen on new moon nights — check lunar calendar.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning on Koh Rong Samloem — wake up early for a peaceful sunrise walk along the beach. Take a last swim or snorkel in the crystal-clear waters. Explore the jungle trail that crosses the island to the less-visited Long Beach (Sunset Beach) on the western side — a 30-minute hike through tropical forest to a completely deserted stretch of white sand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Take the afternoon ferry back to Sihanoukville. Depending on your onward flight schedule, either head directly to Phnom Penh International Airport (approximately 3.5–4 hours by road) or spend time in Sihanoukville before departure. Do some last-minute souvenir shopping — Kampot pepper, silk products, and Angkor-motif artwork make excellent gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Cambodia — reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through ancient temples, moving history, vibrant culture, and paradise beaches. Safe travels!

meals.breakfast: Final island breakfast at your bungalow — fresh tropical fruit, eggs, and Cambodian coffee. Savor the peaceful beach atmosphere one last time.
meals.lunch: Quick lunch in Sihanoukville before the journey to Phnom Penh — local Khmer noodles or a sandwich. Budget: $4–7.
meals.dinner: Airport dinner or a final meal in Phnom Penh if time allows — try a last bowl of samlor machu (Cambodian sour soup) or lok lak beef. Budget: $8–12.

day_by_day.notes: Allow plenty of time for the journey from Sihanoukville to Phnom Penh International Airport — at least 4–5 hours including buffer time. Consider booking a private taxi for reliability (~$50–60). Confirm your return flight details and check-in requirements. Cambodia's 10-day journey covers incredible diversity — from the world's greatest temple complex to colonial history, riverside towns, and tropical island paradise.

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium Cambodia Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

hotel.name: Angkor Archaeological Park, Siem Reap Boutique Stay

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Siem Reap International Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Private luxury transfer arranged to Boutique Stay in Angkor Archaeological Park area.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check-in and settle into your boutique luxury property. Enjoy a welcome drink and orientation with your personal concierge. Take a leisurely stroll through the hotel gardens to decompress from travel. Optional: a rejuvenating 60-minute Khmer herbal welcome massage at the in-house spa.
day_by_day.evening: Private tuk-tuk ride to the atmospheric Pub Street area and Old Market (Psar Chas) for a gentle first evening introduction to Siem Reap. Enjoy sunset cocktails at a rooftop bar overlooking the town before a refined dinner.

meals.breakfast: N/A — in-flight or airport meal
meals.lunch: Light refreshments upon arrival at the hotel — fresh tropical fruit platter, iced lemongrass tea, and Cambodian spring rolls served by the pool
meals.dinner: Dinner at Mahob Restaurant or Cuisine Wat Damnak — a celebrated fine-dining restaurant offering contemporary Cambodian tasting menus with local seasonal ingredients and wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Ensure private airport transfer is pre-booked. Confirm spa appointment in advance. Keep Day 1 relaxed to adjust to the time zone. November is peak dry season in Cambodia — expect warm, sunny weather around 28–32°C.

day_by_day.morning: Pre-dawn wake-up for a private sunrise experience at Angkor Wat — one of the world's most iconic moments. Arrive before 5:30 AM with a personal expert guide. Watch the temple's five towers reflect in the lotus pond as the sky turns gold. Explore the outer galleries, bas-reliefs depicting the Churning of the Ocean of Milk, and the sacred inner sanctum.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Angkor Thom — the great walled city of the Khmer Empire. Visit the Bayon Temple with its 216 enigmatic stone faces, the Elephant Terrace, the Terrace of the Leper King, and Baphuon Temple. Enjoy a private picnic lunch prepared by your hotel in the shade of the ancient grounds.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the hotel for a rest and freshen up. Evening visit to Ta Prohm — the 'Tomb Raider' temple — at dusk when crowds thin and the jungle atmosphere is most evocative. Dinner at the hotel's signature restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Pre-dawn light breakfast box prepared by the hotel — croissants, fresh fruit, coffee thermos, and yogurt to enjoy at sunrise
meals.lunch: Private gourmet picnic lunch arranged by the hotel concierge, served in a shaded pavilion near Angkor Thom — includes Khmer sandwiches, cold brew, tropical fruit, and local sweets
meals.dinner: Dinner at your boutique hotel's signature restaurant — curated Khmer tasting menu with amok fish, lok lak beef, and mango sticky rice dessert

day_by_day.notes: Pre-purchase a 3-day Angkor Archaeological Park pass (approximately $62 USD). Hire a certified private guide for the full day (~$50–80 USD). Bring sunscreen, a hat, comfortable walking shoes, and modest clothing (shoulders and knees covered) to enter temples.

day_by_day.morning: Explore the lesser-visited but spectacular temples of the Angkor region — begin with Preah Khan, a sprawling temple-monastery built by Jayavarman VII. Then visit Neak Pean, a mystical island temple set in an artificial lake, and Ta Som, a smaller gem wrapped in tree roots.
day_by_day.afternoon: Head to the East Mebon and Pre Rup temples — stunning examples of Khmer pyramid-temple architecture with sweeping views from their upper tiers. Enjoy the relative solitude of these off-the-beaten-path sites. Return to the hotel for a poolside afternoon break with refreshments.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private Apsara dance performance — arrange a private cultural dinner show at a traditional Khmer pavilion where trained dancers perform ancient court dances in elaborate gold costumes. This UNESCO-recognized art form is one of Cambodia's greatest cultural treasures.

meals.breakfast: Full à la carte breakfast at the hotel — Eggs Benedict, fresh-pressed juices, Cambodian rice porridge (bobor), tropical fruit platter, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Lunch at Viroth's Restaurant in Siem Reap — elegant garden setting with refined Cambodian cuisine, known for their fish amok and green mango salad
meals.dinner: Traditional Khmer royal banquet dinner served during the private Apsara performance — multi-course spread of Khmer royal cuisine including stuffed lemongrass, grilled river prawns, and coconut desserts

day_by_day.notes: Book the private Apsara performance well in advance through your hotel concierge. Temples are quieter in the afternoon but midday heat can be intense — carry plenty of water. The Angkor 3-day pass covers all temples visited today.

day_by_day.morning: Private sunrise hot-air balloon flight over the Angkor Archaeological Park — a breathtaking bird's-eye perspective of the temple complex, jungle canopy, and Tonlé Sap lake in the distance. Flights typically last 30–45 minutes and are operated by Angkor Balloon at dawn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Artisans Angkor workshop and boutique — a social enterprise training Cambodian youth in traditional Khmer crafts including silk weaving, lacquerware, stone carving, and silver work. Take a guided behind-the-scenes tour. Browse and purchase premium handcrafted souvenirs. Then visit the Angkor National Museum for a deep-dive into Khmer civilization, art, and history.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset cocktails at a rooftop venue overlooking the Angkor skyline. Evening at leisure — explore the vibrant night market or enjoy a private couples' spa treatment at the hotel.

meals.breakfast: Light pre-balloon breakfast at the hotel — fresh fruit, granola, yogurt, and coffee. Full breakfast upon return.
meals.lunch: Lunch at Embassy Restaurant in Siem Reap — sophisticated setting in a colonial-era building with modern Cambodian-French fusion cuisine
meals.dinner: Dinner at Malis Restaurant — one of Siem Reap's most acclaimed fine-dining establishments, serving elevated Cambodian cuisine in a stunning garden setting with an extensive wine list

day_by_day.notes: Hot-air balloon flights are weather-dependent — have a backup activity planned. Book the balloon experience at least 2–3 days in advance. The Angkor National Museum charges a separate entry fee (~$12 USD). Artisans Angkor shopping makes for excellent, ethically-sourced gifts.

day_by_day.morning: Day trip to Banteay Srei — the 'Citadel of Women,' considered the jewel of Khmer art. Located 25 km north of Siem Reap, this 10th-century temple is renowned for its extraordinarily intricate pink sandstone carvings. Travel by private air-conditioned vehicle with your expert guide.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue to Banteay Samré, a beautifully preserved and undervisited temple nearby. Then stop at the Cambodian Landmine Museum — a sobering and important cultural experience highlighting Cambodia's recent history and ongoing de-mining efforts. Return to Siem Reap via the scenic countryside.
day_by_day.evening: Private cooking class with a celebrated local chef — learn to prepare three traditional Khmer dishes from scratch, including a trip to the local market to select fresh ingredients. Enjoy your creations as dinner.

meals.breakfast: Full hotel breakfast before departure — Khmer noodle soup (kuy teav), fresh baguette with local honey, tropical fruits, and specialty coffee
meals.lunch: Picnic-style lunch prepared by the hotel and enjoyed in the gardens of Banteay Srei — includes fresh baguettes, Cambodian cold cuts, fruit, and chilled water
meals.dinner: Your own creations from the private cooking class — typically includes fish amok steamed in banana leaf, Khmer red curry, and banana blossom salad, paired with local Cambodian craft beer or wine

day_by_day.notes: Banteay Srei is covered by the Angkor pass if you have a 7-day pass; otherwise a separate entry fee applies. The Landmine Museum requests a donation. Cooking classes should be booked through the hotel concierge 1–2 days in advance. Dress modestly for temple visits.

day_by_day.morning: Private boat excursion on Tonlé Sap Lake — Southeast Asia's largest freshwater lake and a UNESCO Biosphere Reserve. Depart from Chong Kneas or Kampong Phluk floating village. Explore the extraordinary floating villages where entire communities live on water — schools, temples, restaurants, and homes all built on stilts or floating platforms.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a flooded mangrove forest by kayak or small boat — a unique ecosystem experience. Stop at a local family home for a cultural exchange and traditional Khmer tea. Return to Siem Reap and spend the afternoon at leisure — pool time, spa, or shopping at the Angkor Night Market.
day_by_day.evening: Exclusive private dinner at a heritage Khmer villa — some boutique operators offer private chef dinners in beautifully restored colonial or traditional Khmer homes, creating an intimate and unforgettable dining experience.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast — fresh smoothie bowls, eggs your way, Cambodian iced coffee, and local pastries
meals.lunch: Fresh seafood lunch on the boat or at a floating restaurant on Tonlé Sap Lake — grilled river fish, steamed prawns, morning glory stir-fry, and coconut water
meals.dinner: Private heritage villa dinner — five-course Khmer royal cuisine menu prepared by a personal chef, served by candlelight with curated wine pairings

day_by_day.notes: Tonlé Sap Lake is at its highest and most impressive in November — ideal timing. Choose a reputable operator for the boat tour to ensure an ethical and authentic experience. Book the private villa dinner at least 3 days ahead through your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Private chartered flight or luxury vehicle transfer from Siem Reap to Sihanoukville (approximately 1-hour flight or 6-hour drive — flight strongly recommended for luxury travel). Check into a premium beachfront resort on Otres Beach or Koh Rong Samloem island.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrival and check-in at your luxury beach resort. Spend the afternoon unwinding on pristine white-sand beaches. Enjoy a beachside massage, snorkeling in crystal-clear waters, or simply relax with a cocktail under a palm-thatched umbrella.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset beach cocktails on the shore. Seafood barbecue dinner on the beach — freshly caught lobster, prawns, and fish grilled to perfection under the stars.

meals.breakfast: Light breakfast at the hotel before departure — pastries, fresh fruit, and coffee
meals.lunch: In-flight snack or arrival welcome lunch at the beach resort — fresh seafood platter, tropical salads, and chilled coconut water
meals.dinner: Private beachside seafood barbecue at the resort — whole grilled lobster, tiger prawns, sea bass, and Cambodian dipping sauces, paired with chilled white wine and tropical cocktails

day_by_day.notes: Book the charter flight well in advance — operators include Sky Angkor Airlines or private charter services. Alternatively, a luxury SUV transfer (6 hours) can be arranged. Koh Rong Samloem offers more secluded, pristine beaches and is highly recommended for the luxury beach experience.

day_by_day.morning: Private speedboat island-hopping excursion — explore the stunning archipelago surrounding Koh Rong. Visit secluded bays, hidden lagoons, and uninhabited islands. Snorkeling stop at a pristine coral reef teeming with tropical fish, sea turtles, and vibrant marine life.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the resort for a luxurious spa afternoon — indulge in a 2-hour Khmer traditional massage and body scrub using local ingredients like turmeric, jasmine, and coconut. Relax by the infinity pool overlooking the turquoise sea.
day_by_day.evening: Bioluminescent plankton night swim — a magical natural phenomenon visible in the waters around Koh Rong Samloem. Wade into the warm sea and watch the water glow electric blue around your movements. Return for a candlelit dinner at the resort's fine-dining restaurant.

meals.breakfast: Full resort breakfast — tropical fruit buffet, eggs Benedict with smoked salmon, fresh-baked pastries, and specialty coffee overlooking the sea
meals.lunch: Gourmet picnic lunch on a secluded beach during the island-hopping excursion — charcuterie, fresh baguettes, tropical fruits, and chilled rosé wine
meals.dinner: Fine-dining dinner at the resort restaurant — pan-seared grouper with lemongrass beurre blanc, Cambodian lobster bisque, and passion fruit panna cotta, with a curated wine list

day_by_day.notes: Bioluminescent plankton are most visible on moonless nights — check the lunar calendar. The phenomenon is most active June–November, so timing is perfect. Book the spa treatments in advance. Bring reef-safe sunscreen for snorkeling.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise yoga session on the beach led by a private instructor — greet the morning with a 60-minute session as the sun rises over the Gulf of Thailand. Follow with a refreshing ocean swim. Optional: stand-up paddleboarding or kayaking along the coastline.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the fishing village of Koh Rong for a cultural immersion — meet local fishermen, learn about traditional fishing techniques, and visit a small community school. Return to the resort for final beach time. Pack and prepare for departure back to Siem Reap or Phnom Penh.
day_by_day.evening: Return flight or transfer back to Siem Reap. Farewell dinner at one of Siem Reap's finest restaurants — a celebratory meal to mark the penultimate evening of your Cambodia journey.

meals.breakfast: Light post-yoga breakfast — acai bowls, green smoothies, tropical fruit, and herbal teas
meals.lunch: Farewell lunch at the beach resort — Cambodian seafood curry, fresh papaya salad, and coconut ice cream
meals.dinner: Celebratory farewell dinner at Cuisine Wat Damnak in Siem Reap — Cambodia's most acclaimed fine-dining experience, offering a five-course seasonal tasting menu with wine pairings that showcases the full depth of Khmer culinary tradition

day_by_day.notes: Arrange the return flight or transfer in advance. If returning to Siem Reap, plan to arrive by late afternoon to allow time to freshen up before dinner. Cuisine Wat Damnak requires advance reservations — book at least 3–5 days ahead.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Siem Reap — a peaceful sunrise walk or bicycle ride through the quiet lanes surrounding Angkor Wat for one last magical encounter with the temples. Visit Phnom Bakheng hill temple for panoramic views of the Angkor plain and Tonlé Sap Lake glittering in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return to the hotel for checkout. Last-minute luxury shopping at Artisans Angkor or the Senteurs d'Angkor boutique for premium Cambodian crafts, silks, spices, and beauty products. Private transfer to Siem Reap International Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Siem Reap. Reflect on an extraordinary 10-day journey through one of Asia's most historically rich and culturally vibrant destinations.

meals.breakfast: Final hotel breakfast — full spread of both Western and Cambodian options, including kuy teav noodle soup, fresh tropical fruits, eggs, pastries, and Cambodian iced coffee
meals.lunch: Light farewell lunch at the hotel or a nearby café — Khmer chicken sandwich, fresh spring rolls, and a signature mango smoothie
meals.dinner: Airport lounge dining or in-flight meal

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 3 hours before departure for airport check-in. Store purchased artworks and fragile items carefully in checked luggage. Tip your guides, drivers, and hotel staff generously — gratuity is an important part of the local economy. Carry USD cash for tips and small purchases throughout the trip.
